messages:
daria: heads up — noticed a small but consistent customer report: streaming sessions that flip routes during a probe window are creating duplicate billing events. :thinking:
jonathan: do we have a repro or logs? which probe? server or proxy?
ops-bot: ALERT: tenant=acme reconnect_rate=320/min snapshot=2026-05-20T18:05:21Z
maria: quick context — this popped up after the proxy keepalive rollout (65s -> 45s) + the sticky-routing canary. clients with flaky mobile networks are getting a resume -> route-swap -> reconnect loop.
kevin: is the duplicate billing from the router counting the resumed request and the new connection separately? or from our metering sidecar retrying?
daria: looks like both. The route-swap causes the new connection to be routed to a different pool; resume flow attempts to rehydrate KV cache but fails idempotency check, so the backend replays token-metering hook. logs snippet:
```
[18:05:21Z] resume_id=abc123 route=pool-eu-1 auth=ok resume_attempt=1
[18:05:21Z] new_conn=conn-789 route=pool-us-2 session_swap=true billing_hook=invoke token_count=150
[18:05:22Z] resume-fallback=replay_triggered billing_event_id=evt-555
```
jonathan: ugh. console didn't make this obvious — charts only show per-connection tokens but not aligned to resume_id. we can't trace dedupe across route changes.
alyssa: from a Console UX POV we can add a small 'session lineage' view for streams showing resume_id, route_history, and billing_events. that would have surfaced this immediately. low-effort: expose resume_id as label on the flamegraph.
maria: agree on telemetry. immediate mitigation? lengthen sticky TTL for canary users? or make resume idempotency stronger (have metering ignore events with same resume_id for X seconds)?
kevin: metering dedupe is tricky — we have to ensure we don't undercount legitimate multi-shard splits. Maybe require dedupe only when resume_id matches AND a payload checksum matches. cheap stopgap: if route changes within N seconds of resume, drop the automatic billing hook and surface a manual audit event.
daria: can we patch proxy to keep route affinity for 10s after resume success? that would avoid mid-resume flips caused by recent rollout balancing.
jonathan: that feels safer. also add a console alert rule: if reconnect_rate spikes and route_entropy increases for a tenant, flag as potential billing-dupe risk.
alyssa: I'll add a low-priority UX ticket for session lineage and a dashboard card for resume_id -> billing_event correlation.
maria: Ops mitigation plan — rollback keepalive change for the canary edge group (45s) and re-enable 65s there until we ship dedupe. rolling back just the canary reduces blast radius.
kevin: timeline? I can implement a quick server-side dedupe: require (resume_id + short-window) to suppress duplicate billing events. low risk and quick.
daria: ok let's do two things: (1) rollback keepalive on canary edge now, (2) kevin, please prepare a hotfix for dedupe based on resume_id+checksum with 30s window. alyssa, please add the resume_id visualization and new alert. jonathan, can you add a trace span for route-assignment emitted at decision time?
jonathan: yep — will add route.assign span and tag it with route_pool and lease_revision. that'll help correlate.
ops-bot: RUNBOOK: if billing-dupe alert fires -> revert keepalive canary -> scale down canary edge -> escalate to oncall.
daria: thanks everyone. followups: kevin will post a PR, jonathan will update tracing, alyssa will push dashboard changes. i'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers of a billing adjustment if dedupe can't be retroactive. :+1:
kevin: PR drafted, linking in #eng-releases when ready.
jonathan: trace patch in review.
alyssa: dashboard card + alert rule created in staging. preview link: https://console.internal/redwood/session-lineage?tenant=acme (staging) :eyes:
maria: monitoring shows reconnect_rate dropping after partial rollback on canary. watching.
daria: closing loop — we should also write a short postmortem note for the internal incidents channel after we confirm root cause/dedupe effectiveness.
jonathan: +1
